tonight.text:
ramroomti,

i don't have anything clever to say tonight. i just hope you're okay.

i like that these photos still exist. even the blurry ones. they remind me of ordinary moments i wouldn't want to lose.

you don't have to reply to any of this.

silence.text:
i miss talking to you. the small things as much as the big ones.

i don't know what this space feels like for you, and i don't want to guess. i can care about you and leave you room at the same time.

regret.text:
there are things i wish had gone differently. i don't want to cover that up with a nice sentence.

but the good days were part of us too. i still smile at these pictures. i'm glad we have them.

door.text:
i can't promise what comes next. and i can't speak for you.

if we ever both wanted to try again, i'd want there to be room for the difficult conversations too. not just the things we miss.

for now, this is a place to keep the memories. it doesn't ask you for an answer.

love: the way you say my name
because somehow you could make the most normal sentence sound different just by saying my name.
the sudden switches, the chaos, the little versions of you that appeared out of nowhere.
the way you could completely change the vibe of my day
one message from you could genuinely flip my whole mood.
even the dumb ones. especially the dumb ones.
you never warned me and somehow that made it even better.
the way you made me miss you even when we literally just talked
messages: It feels strange not knowing every little detail of your day anymore. I hope you’re eating well, sleeping on time, and not letting your brain convince you that you’re alone in this world. Even from a distance, I’m rooting for your happiness.
open if you’re wondering if I still care
Of course I do. People don’t just un-love someone who meant this much to them overnight. This whole website is still standing here for a reason.

I miss you too. And no, you’re not being dramatic for feeling it. Go look at one of the pictures above and remember there’s a real person on the other side of that screen who cares about you so fucking much.
Come back to what is actually true, not every scary possibility your brain can invent. Breathe. You don’t have to solve everything tonight.
open when you feel like you’re bothering me
You were never a burden to me. Even now, if something is heavy on your mind, you never have to hesitate.
open when you’re mad at me
Okay. Be mad. I’d always rather honesty than silence. When the dust settles, grace is always waiting here.
Put the phone down for a second, breathe slowly, unclench your jaw. You’re safe, and you can rest now.
open when you want to smile
Look at the pictures where we clearly had no idea what we were doing 😭 you’re welcome.

girl: the girl I couldn’t stop thinking about

There was a girl who kept appearing in a boy’s thoughts at the most inconvenient times. While he was eating. While he was trying to sleep. While he was pretending to pay attention. He eventually realized the problem wasn’t that he couldn’t stop thinking about her. It was that he didn’t want to.
boy: ramroomti and the boy who loved her

Once there was a girl named ramroomti and a boy who somehow got very attached to her. They laughed at stupid things, annoyed each other, missed each other, and kept finding their way back to the same little corner of the world. The boy never needed a perfect ending. He just wanted more chapters with her.
night: the night they finally fell asleep together

One night, after all the talking and overthinking and pretending they weren’t tired, they finally went quiet. No fixing anything. No figuring anything out. Just two people close enough to hear each other breathe. And for once, that was enough.
bridge: the two people who grew and found their way back

Sometimes two people who love each other deeply hit a season where the world gets too loud and they have to step back to breathe. The boy didn’t burn the bridge—he just left a lantern on it. Because real stories don’t always end when a chapter closes; sometimes they just pause until both hearts are ready for the next page.

triggers: I still catch my thumb hovering over the share button before I remember—and I just smile and hope you’d have laughed at it too.
Certain songs come on the aux and for three minutes it feels like no time has passed at all.
You’re still the first person my brain wants to tell whenever something random or exciting happens in my day.
Amman feels a little different when every other street has a memory attached to it.
That hour when the whole house is asleep and we used to talk about everything and nothing.
Still remembering your exact order by heart without even trying.
